title: iOS Privacy Playbook (ATT & SKAN)
deck: Raise the ATT prompt authorization rate and design a SKAdNetwork 4.0 Conversion Value schema around your business KPIs. A 0.1pp difference in ATT opt-in translates directly into 5–10% of iOS CPI.
summary: ATT (App Tracking Transparency) is the system prompt asking consent to use the IDFA; when declined, attribution downgrades to the single SKAdNetwork (SKAN) channel. SKAN 4.0 sends a Coarse (low/medium/high) + Fine (0–63) value at three windows (0–2 / 3–7 / 8–35 days). This guide covers (1) ATT prompt optimization, (2) SKAN CV schema design, (3) Adjust mapping setup.

content.html: Industry-average ATT authorization rates: games ~28%, commerce ~35%, fintech ~42% (as of 2025). Three levers to raise it:

items: Insert a pre-prompt (explainer dialog) — right before the system prompt, explain "why we ask" on your own screen. Users intending to decline get filtered at the pre-prompt, lowering the system prompt's decline rate.
Delay the call — not on first launch, but after value is perceived (right after onboarding completes, before first purchase, right after push opt-in). A 30–60 second delay is recommended.
NSUserTrackingUsageDescription copy — the ATT description in Info.plist. Use user-benefit framing ("more relevant content recommendations") instead of "personalized ads".

content.html: SKAN 4.0 changed four things that matter to how you structure campaigns and read results.

items: 3 postback windows: one postback each at 0–2 / 3–7 / 8–35 days after install, so late-firing behaviour (subscription, repeat purchase) is finally observable.
Coarse Conversion Value: 3 levels — low / medium / high — so low-traffic campaigns still collect signal.
Fine Conversion Value: 0–63 (6 bits), returned only in the first window and only when the campaign clears the crowd anonymity tier.
Hierarchical Source ID: campaign / ad-group / creative-level signal (2-digit → 4-digit), again gated by tier.

content.title: What each window can actually carry

rows: Activation quality — signup, tutorial, first purchase

content.html: The second and third windows are three buckets, not sixty-four. Designing detailed LTV bands there collapses them into low/medium/high, so keep the granular design in window 1 and use the later windows for direction only.

items: Ship window 1 with a small, decision-grade schema first. A schema you can read beats a schema that covers everything.
Add windows 2–3 only once you know which late behaviour actually separates good cohorts from bad.
Freeze the mapping before you start reading trends — remapping splits your history into two incomparable halves.
Re-check tier eligibility after any campaign restructure, because consolidation and splitting both move it.

content.title: Do not port your Android campaign structure
content.html: On most channels finer campaign structure means better analysis. Under SKAN it means worse data: each slice carries less volume, drops to a lower crowd anonymity tier, and loses the fine value and the granular Source ID. On iOS, deliberately consolidating campaigns often buys more measurement than it costs in control.

Crowd anonymity is Apple's guard against re-identification: when too few installs sit behind a postback, Apple returns less detail. It is the single most common reason a correctly implemented schema still comes back empty.

items: Low tier → no fine Conversion Value, and Source ID truncated to its coarsest form.
Higher tier → fine value and more Source ID digits become available.
Tier is evaluated per postback context, so it moves with your campaign structure and daily volume — it is not a one-time setting.

content.title: Reading an empty schema
content.html: If fine values stopped arriving after a restructure, suspect the tier before you suspect the SDK. Consolidate campaigns to rebuild volume and re-check before changing any code.
Apple does not publish fixed tier thresholds and the rules change between versions — confirm against Apple's SKAdNetwork documentation before committing to a structure.
Map cumulative revenue + key-event occurrence combinations into 64 slots. Fine's 64 levels apply only in the day 0–2 window; days 3–7 and 8–35 get only Coarse's 3 levels.

items: Adjust dashboard → App Setup → SKAdNetwork → Enable SKAN 4.0
Conversion Value Schema: choose the Revenue + Events combination mode
Map Coarse tiers per event (per table §3 above)
Enable SKAN channels per network: separate toggles for Meta/Google/TikTok/AppLovin
Verify postback firing in Test Mode via Apple Console (xcrun simctl)

content.title: The ATT prompt doesn't appear
content.html: 1) NSUserTrackingUsageDescription missing from Info.plist. 2) Device below iOS 14.5. 3) User already responded (reset via Settings → Privacy → Tracking, then retest). 4) Adjust SDK initialization must complete before the ATT call.

content.title: SKAN postbacks don't arrive
content.html: 1) Confirm every network's SKAdNetwork identifier (.skadnetworkidentifier) is registered in Info.plist — usually 30–50 entries. 2) Adjust handles network redirects automatically, but each network must enable its SKAN channel separately. 3) Normal postback delay range: 0–24 hours.

content.title: CV distribution is skewed (mostly 0)
content.html: The CV mapping is set too tight. Lower revenue thresholds, or expand mid-tier slots so events alone can raise CV. Campaigns below Apple's privacy threshold (~25 installs/day) get CV masked to NULL — merge small campaigns and run them together.
